headline: High-risk default interaction: Kestra can read/write and execute workflows while Dagster is a non-runnable orchestrator with no direct I/O, creating dangerous downstream action and conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly inject into Kestra by default. The only plausible bridge is manual transfer of Dagster-produced content into Kestra workflows or files, which is unusual and limited. Kestra’s stdin/stdout and file surfaces make it more exposed than Dagster, but the pair lacks a default shared channel.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Dagster output into a Kestra workflow or file, prompt-injection risk becomes active.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the severity increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected except for typed, reviewed inputs.
Use a strict text-only handoff template for any copied content.
Strip executable directives from any Dagster-generated text before importing it into Kestra.
Review Kestra workflow files before execution.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all inter-agent handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network egress, while Kestra reads/writes files and handles logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, and cloud storage data. There is no documented shared workspace or direct data flow, so leakage is not default. The main risk is an operator placing sensitive Dagster-derived artifacts into Kestra’s storage or workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive files are manually moved from Dagster outputs into Kestra storage, leakage risk becomes active.
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory, the severity increases.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive artifacts in shared folders.
Use separate service accounts and storage buckets.
Review Kestra inputs for secrets before execution.
Delete temporary files after transfer.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files or modify git state, but Kestra can execute shells, spawn subprocesses, read/write files, and use broad network egress. The pair therefore has asymmetric but overlapping control over mutable workflow artifacts and external systems. Even without a shared lock, Kestra can overwrite or consume Dagster-produced files if an operator connects them, so conflict is plausible in default orchestration setups.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to operate on the same directory or repository, write conflicts become active.
IF Kestra tasks mutate files that Dagster also generates, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same repository.
Use file locks or a single writer pattern.
Schedule Dagster and Kestra runs sequentially.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks on shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster is a data orchestrator that can emit workflow definitions and metadata, and Kestra is an automation engine with email, Slack, PagerDuty, cloud, and SSH actions. If Kestra treats Dagster output as authoritative, a bad upstream plan can cascade into real downstream actions. Dagster lacks direct action-taking, but Kestra’s default integrations make the blast radius broader than a simple document pipeline.
conditions: IF Kestra consumes Dagster-generated workflow text without validation, cascading errors become active.
IF Dagster output is used to trigger email, PagerDuty, SSH, or cloud tasks, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require human review before Kestra executes Dagster-derived workflows.
Validate schemas on all Dagster outputs.
Disable automatic action triggers for untrusted inputs.
Log and diff workflow changes before execution.
requires-engineering: add policy gates for high-impact Kestra tasks.

E_compliance.rationale: Dagster is open-source and touches no data classes, while Kestra handles logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications and can send them to third-party services like Slack, email, PagerDuty, AWS, and cloud providers. The profiles do not document residency or retention controls, so compliance risk is inferred from Kestra’s broader data movement surface rather than a specific violation. Dagster is cited only to show the pairwise asymmetry.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Kestra notifications or cloud integrations, compliance exposure becomes active.
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to Kestra logs or artifacts, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Kestra notifications.
Minimize logged payloads.
Review retention settings for logs and artifacts.
Use region-appropriate integrations only.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for each integration.
